1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter spacing and ample line spacing on every screen.

2.why: Instructions appear in regular sentence-case prose with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs.

3.why: The centered single-column card layout with large inputs and buttons is clearly designed to remain readable at mobile widths.

4.why: All instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as “Enter the six-digit identity code” and “Each recovery code works once.”

5.why: Placeholders give format hints for recovery codes and “6 digits” for OTP fields, but the identity-code field shows no example of the expected input.

6.why: No screen presents a long block of text; every step can be completed after reading only one or two short sentences.

7.why: Secrets and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text that can be copied, although no dedicated copy buttons are provided.

8.why: Despite copy mentioning “scanning a code,” no QR code or equivalent visual alternative is ever displayed—only the raw secret string.

9.why: Ordinary input fields are used (so browser autofill may work for email/phone), yet no evidence of password-manager or one-time-code autofill support appears for secrets or OTP fields.

10.why: Clear page headings name the current step and the primary action is always a prominent full-width blue button.

11.why: Enrolment screens focus on one main CTA at a time, though the authenticator-confirm screen collects both the secret and a code together and settings offers several peer actions.

12.why: Success feedback such as “Authenticator verification succeeded” and “Recovery code accepted and permanently consumed” states what happened; next-step guidance is sometimes only implicit.

13.why: Users can retry failed verification, start over, and regenerate recovery codes without penalty, but no reveal/hide controls for codes are present.

14.why: The only observed error message—“The request could not be completed”—is generic, does not explain the cause, and gives no recovery guidance.

15.why: No timers, countdowns, or expiry warnings appear on any screen, so reading and code entry are unlimited.
